notes: Parts are unchanged from step 1; no parts added or dropped.

Breadboard naming follows the catalogue: bank 't' is rows a-e and bank 'b' is rows f-j. In the image the rows a-e half is drawn at the bottom and f-j at the top. The button straddles the centre gap in columns 10 and 12, with its top legs in bank b (row g) and its bottom legs in bank t (row d).

The pushbutton's legs are mapped so that side 1 is the column-10 pair (1.l in 10b, 1.r in 10t) and side 2 is the column-12 pair (2.l in 12b, 2.r in 12t). This is the orientation in which pressing the button joins pin 2 (column 10) to GND (column 12), as the schematic shows. The image shows only the legs, so the l/r labels are an assumption.

The teal wire runs from digital pin 2 to hole 10t.c. The black wire runs from a GND socket in the power header to hole 12t.c. The image shows the second GND socket next to VIN, so it is mapped to GND.2.
No external resistor is used. The internal pull-up on pin 2 is enabled in software (INPUT_PULLUP). The LED on pin 13 is the onboard LED, not a separate part.
The USB cable to the computer for serial is not drawn in the circuit image and is not in the parts list, so it is not modelled.
